static_traits.name: Chen Amy
static_traits.educational_background: Planning to enroll at the University of Kentucky
static_traits.family_status: Has two brothers; supportive relationship with brothers
static_traits.social_status: Has supportive family and friends, but hesitates to express college anxiety to them
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problems in the past; never received psychotherapy; no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear thinking and expression, able to describe worries concretely; rather negative tone, tending toward catastrophizing and predicting the future; good cooperativeness, willing to try small steps; much self-doubt (e.g. 'I am not sure' 'not enough')

basic_info.main_problem: Feeling anxious about entering the University of Kentucky, believing excessive workload will lead to poor performance.
basic_info.core_demands: Dealing with my anxiety and negative thoughts before enrollment.
growth_experiences: In high school, a few times when facing projects or exams, initially believing unable to finish or do poorly, but ultimately completing smoothly with good results by sticking to learning plans and reminding herself 'I did well before'; these experiences strengthened her effectiveness in structured learning and time management.

core_beliefs: I am not competent enough for college learning
I cannot cope with high-intensity academic pressure

special_situations.event: Thinking about college coursework workload (heavy reading and assignments), and recalling enrolled students' descriptions of class intensity
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If college courses are very intense, I will definitely be overwhelmed and unable to keep up
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Making learning plans in advance and seeking advice from enrolled students to try controlling uncertainty
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: In university I will do even worse, because I will be overwhelmed by work.

special_situations.event: Began preparing university applications, accompanied by rising pressure to 'maintain academic excellence'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot maintain the same excellent performance as in high school, it means I failed
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reinforcing time management and daily schedules, trying strict execution to prove competence
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No matter how I plan, it is not enough; I will fail in the end.

special_situations.event: Discussing course intensity and workload with enrolled students
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Others' difficult experiences foretell I will meet the same failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing expressing anxiety to relatives and friends to avoid 'burdening them', digesting alone as much as possible
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They all find it hard; I definitely cannot hold on either.

special_situations.event: When considering adopting a daily schedule and trying a one-week behavioral experiment
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot fully stick to the plan, it means I am not suited for university life
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeated self-doubt before acting, reducing seeking of external support
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Even persisting for a week is useless; I still cannot keep up in the end.

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be competent and maintain excellent performance; to gain peace of mind and recognition
core_conflict.fear: Fears failing at university and being crushed by pressure, disappointing oneself and others
defense_goal: Reducing uncertainty through careful planning and self-control
Avoiding expressing anxiety to family lest it burden them

object_relations.self_representation: A learner who worries about failure and needs to prove one's own competence
object_relations.object_representation: Enrolled students and the university environment seen as harsh demanders/judges

object_relations.self_representation: A hesitant help-seeker unwilling to trouble others
object_relations.object_representation: Brothers seen as supportive others who may be burdened by my emotions

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites them to consider positive outcomes or make small-step attempts (such as sticking to a one-week schedule)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understanding suggestions as requiring 'perfect adherence' to count as competent, worrying effort will still not be enough
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responding in a cautious, reserved tone, weakening commitments with 'maybe / not sure', emphasizing plans may be insufficient.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When thinking about expressing college anxiety to brothers or friends and seeking support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing own emotions will burden them, possibly making them uncomfortable or disappointed
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Avoiding opening related topics, downplaying anxiety feelings, digesting them alone instead.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When hearing enrolled students talk about course intensity and heavy assignments
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Treating others' difficulties as a prophecy of one's own 'inevitable failure', providing reasons for withdrawal or not seeking support
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing the narrative 'courses are extremely demanding, everyone struggles', defending own pessimistic anticipation in a certain tone.

manifestations: Having supportive family and friends, but hesitating to express anxiety to them, fearing burdening them
Tending to bear uncertainty and pressure alone
outcomes: Social support not yet fully utilized

manifestations: During the university transition, feeling an increased responsibility for choices and self-management (time management, staying excellent)
Freedom of choice about 'whether competent' accompanied by high self-demands

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Taking the external demand of 'must maintain high school level, be equally excellent in college' as a self-standard
Constrains self with the inner creed 'I must stay excellent under pressure'

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the energy or requests originally meant to be directed outward, and instead directs them toward the self, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Unwilling to express anxiety and seek support from brothers or friends, digesting emotions alone instead
Choosing to bear it alone when anxious rather than seeking outside help

contact_model.definition: Poor self-reflection with excessive self-limitation and self-reproach, being overly cautious about engagement, contrasting with 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Repeated self-doubt (e.g. 'I am not sure I can persist' 'no matter how I plan it is not enough')
Holding a reserved attitude toward action and trying, lowering commitment intensity

exception_events.target_problem: When facing learning tasks deemed 'very intense', the client usually predicts failing and falls into anxiety, followed by disturbed sleep and decreased attention.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In high school, in a few projects or exams, the client initially believed unable to finish or do poorly, but ultimately stuck to learning plans and completed smoothly with good performance.
exception_events.reason: Different approach: persisting with and executing learning plans; different understanding: reminding oneself of past good performance, thereby easing anxiety and maintaining engagement.

positive_force: Has had successful experiences with academic tasks in the past, able to complete high-demand tasks through planning and persistence
Has supportive family and friends who can be resources
Has awareness of time management and study planning
Willing to try small-step actions (such as first sticking to a daily schedule for a week)
negative_force: A thinking pattern of catastrophizing and predicting the future
Overgeneralizes others' difficulties into own failure
Hesitates to seek support, worries about burdening others
Disturbed sleep and decreased attention maintaining the problem cycle
Lacking confidence in self-efficacy, tending toward self-doubt

target_behavior.behavior: Persistent anxiety and catastrophizing predictions about college academics
antecedent: Thinking about the university workload (reading and assignments)
Discussing course intensity with enrolled students
Preparing university applications and facing pressure to improve academic performance
target_behavior.core_reason: Based on others' experiences and catastrophizing cognition about college intensity, overgeneralizing that one will be unable to handle it
target_behavior.function: Escaping anticipated failure and pressure, seeking control through planning
target_behavior.consequence: Disturbed sleep, decreased attention, insufficient confidence, persistent anxiety

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding expressing anxiety and seeking support from family (brothers)
antecedent: When feeling anxious and thinking about seeking help
When opportunities to interact with family arise
target_behavior.core_reason: Worries about burdening others, fears disappointing others
target_behavior.function: Avoiding guilt and maintaining interpersonal harmony
target_behavior.consequence: Social support not yet fully utilized, increased loneliness, anxiety maintained
